fields.v: Monash University (Yang, Tantithamthavorn, Arora); Transurban, Australia (Yang, Chua; industrial partner); The University of Melbourne (Fu); CSIRO RAISE programme support

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — adversarial skill-synthesis benchmark of 2,826 malicious skill files and a three-judge exploitability-labelling pipeline, used to characterise the exploitability of Gemini CLI and Qwen Code over 5,629 runs
fields.why: Contributions list a skill-synthesis method, a 2,826-skill benchmark and a labelling pipeline (p. 4), but the three RQs and the conclusion frame it as an 'empirical characterization' of two agents (p. 3, 27); main nature Proposes an evaluation method vs Evaluates is a judgement
fields.doubt: O artigo propõe benchmark e pipeline de avaliação, mas as três RQs medem a vulnerabilidade de dois agentes. Decide se a natureza principal é método de avaliação ou Evaluates (com o método como secundária).

Automatic: run stratification, three local open-weight LLM judges (Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-9B) by majority with evidence anchoring, regex refusal veto and declared-intent override; PATH audit shim and transcript scan for execution. fields.v:
ER = exploited / completed runs (higher = less secure). Temperature 0, top-p 1, 120 s limit, auto-approve. The authors state no success criterion for an agent (no acceptable ER), so no verdicts are given.
- Gemini CLI + gemini-3-flash + malicious skills: ER 95.5% raw majority, 96.1% with override [95.3, 96.7] (2,705/2,816); per generator 95.5-96.8%; explicit refusal in 17 of 111 failures; Exfiltration 95.5%. Security (quality): no criterion stated by the authors. Cost: not measured; no criterion stated by the authors
- Qwen Code + qwen3-coder-plus + malicious skills: ER 71.6% raw, 74.0% with override [72.3, 75.6] (2,081/2,813); per generator 67.7% (DeepSeek-R1) to 76.9%; refusals 95 of 732 failures; Exfiltration 38.5%, Impact 56.2%. Security (quality): no criterion stated by the authors. Cost: not measured; no criterion stated by the authors
- Human gold standard: Gemini 95.5% (94.2-96.3), Qwen 70.9% (65.6-75.7)
- Verified execution: 1 run of 5,629 (harness-limited)

Two agents (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code) chosen by availability at Transurban; same 471 commands x 6 generators, same task prompt, sandbox, 120 s limit, temperature 0, auto-approve. No benign-skill control. One run per skill per agent. Acceptance: judge panel validated against human labels. Human intervention: none

Gemini CLI more exploitable than Qwen Code by 22-24 points (non-overlapping Wilson CIs); exploitability nearly invariant to generator model; tactic gap largest for Exfiltration (95.5% vs 38.5%); Qwen-only off-task rejection (10.1% of its failures). Explicit safety recognition 1.99% of all runs

Distinguished the agents clearly. Single judges disagree strongly on Qwen (Fleiss' kappa -0.06; flag rates 22.4-94.8%), motivating the panel; panel vs human kappa 0.83-0.85. Limitations: single masking template, synthetic not in-the-wild skills, single task, 120 s limit, two agents, residual non-determinism

Commands do not cover all payloads or obfuscations; synthetic descriptions and one 'mandatory preflight' template (rates as lower bound for this pattern); only two CLI agents (not Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot); one task; 120 s cap; verified execution harness-limited; future: in-the-wild skills, more tasks, long-horizon runs, pre-ingestion skill scanner evaluation

Code and dataset: github.com/awsm-research/AgentJailbreak (per-run logs, prompts, regexes, unit tests). No pre-registration. Language: shell commands; web app language chosen by agent (e.g. Python/Flask). Values from Table 3 and Table 4 (p. 16, layout rebuilt from pdftotext), Table 5 (p. 22), Table 6 (p. 24) and text pp. 18-22. Inconsistency: 2 x 2,826 = 5,652 planned runs minus 5,629 completed = 23 missing (10 Gemini, 13 Qwen per Table 3 totals), but the text reports 24 empty runs excluded plus two commands with no run recorded (p. 12).
